topic: Research-first sakura model for the Japanese campus garden
model: Prunus × yedoensis, Yoshino / pale-pink Akebono inspired late-bloom ornamental planting

sources.title: Types of Trees — Cherry Blossom Festival
facts: Yoshino and Akebono have round-topped, wide-spreading habits.
Yoshino flowers are single white blossoms in clusters; Akebono single blossoms are pale pink fading toward white.
The guide describes clusters of two to five flowers for these selections.
model_choices: Asymmetric tiered spreading limbs and an open, broad rounded crown.
Small groups of four pale pink-white cupped blossoms distributed along visible woody twigs.

sources.title: Prunus x yedoensis — Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
facts: The canopy is arching, rounded and spreading rather than a conical crown.
Flowers are cup-shaped with four to five petals and white to pink coloration.
Leaves are alternate, simple, ovate or elliptical with serrated margins.
The bark has prominent horizontal lenticels.
model_choices: Nearby native flowers have five separate notched and physically cupped petal surfaces, pink receptacle and small golden stamens; distant individual surfaces preserve this five-petal shape through an analytical alpha mask.
Sparse young green-bronze serrated leaves represent late bloom, not a midsummer mass of green foliage.
Locally generated reddish-brown bark texture with horizontal lighter lenticel markings.

sources.publisher: Keele University, National Collection of Flowering Cherries
sources.title: About cherries
facts: Cherry twigs bear clusters of buds.
Cherry bark is usually smooth with regularly placed rougher horizontal lenticel lines.
model_choices: Pedicels begin on woody twig surfaces; blossoms are not randomly floating throughout a sphere.
Short forks and tapered branch segments remain visible through small crown openings.

reference_handling: Official source photographs were viewed for research, not copied, redistributed or used as texture assets. Geometry and procedural textures were authored locally.
artistic_adaptations: This is a botanical reference-based ornamental scene model, not a scanned specimen or a named garden replica.
Default campus trees are younger and smaller than fully mature 30–50 foot specimens to fit existing walkable planting beds.
Blossom diameter is deliberately enlarged to approximately 7–10 cm for legibility at campus viewing distance; this is an explicit rendering adaptation, not a botanical measurement.
Reduced-quality modes retain every tree and broaden individual petals slightly to preserve crown coverage while reducing instances.

Distant individual flowers use a locally painted analytical five-petal alpha mask on fixed 3D oriented surfaces. They do not rotate to face the camera; no whole-tree billboard or opaque crown shell is used.
Nearby flowers add real cupped petal and pedicel geometry. Texture alpha testing writes depth normally and avoids transparency sorting.

rendering.coverage_note: Coverage is a CPU alpha-aware projection of the actual generated model, not a browser/GPU performance or photorealism claim.
rendering.motion_control: Wind animation uses a pause-aware local clock and is disabled for low and performance presets.
rendering.spatial_batching: v92: exact existing instance samples partitioned per tree with shared geometry/materials/textures for native camera and shadow frustum culling. No per-frame instance uploads.
